jobs.title: Software Engineer - Traffic Capacity & Performance
jobs.description:
Meta's edge network carries traffic in two directions: content out to billions of people from edge sites and caches inside internet service providers, and Meta's own services and AI agents reaching sites across the internet. The Traffic Capacity & Performance team decides how much capacity Meta builds for both, and where. We size it to keep serving through failures and demand spikes, drain sites at peak on purpose to find weak spots before a real outage does, and have apps and services ask for less when capacity runs low.  
  
  

### **Software Engineer - Traffic Capacity & Performance Responsibilities:**

* Build and extend large-scale simulation of global traffic placement: how traffic shifts across edge sites as demand grows and as sites, peering links and backbone paths fail. Run thousands of scenarios fast enough to plan with
* Work with the load-balancing team on simulation fidelity and performance, and validate results against production behavior and live failure tests
* Formulate and solve capacity planning as constrained optimization: where to add compute, peering and caches, given space, power, supply, latency and failure constraints. Build and tune the solvers
* Plan capacity for the browsers, proxies and caches Meta's services and AI agents use to reach the internet, and find which one becomes the bottleneck as Meta's internet access needs grow
* Build production forecasting of peak demand, by region and by product, driven by product changes and events rather than trend alone. Quantify uncertainty and track accuracy against actuals
* Model failures and their impact, including correlated and cascading failures. Size the buffers we hold against failures and demand surges, and express plans as risk and cost trade-offs leadership can choose between
* Build agentic planning systems that rerun forecasts and plans continuously, detect drift, explain what changed and propose actions, with evaluations and guardrails
* Lead technical direction across teams, mentor engineers, and represent capacity engineering in cross-team design reviews

jobs.description:
**What to Expect**

Own the path from line images to a solution Tesla can trust. We collect images on PCBA and TLA lines and developing models that to do this. Your job is to determine what the images can support, prove or kill an approach on our data, and leave us with a solution that works in production, whether that is a model we run, a system we buy, or a clear stop.

You will work with Supplier industrialization engineers, and internal Tesla stakeholders, external solution providers. You will be expected to identify a solution; you will not be handed a labeled dataset or a chosen architecture.

  
**What You'll Do**

* Assess line images for camera, lighting, resolution, and consistency across lines and products, and determine whether defects are visible and separable from normal variation
* Turn the quality problem into a testable vision problem, including which defect is in scope, the acceptable miss rate and false-reject rate, and the cycle time the result must meet
* Build the minimum dataset and labeling approach for rare defects, weak labels, and a large volume of good images
* Select classification, detection, segmentation, or anomaly detection based on the data, not a predetermined architecture
* Run a time-boxed proof on our images, comparing a small set of real options, including classical vision, a trained model, and a commercial AOI or vision system
* Recommend build versus buy, including what data, lighting, or camera changes are required before scaling
* Pilot the chosen approach on one line, covering latency, station integration, traceability, and monitoring
* Validate the chosen system on production data, covering holdout images, line trials, golden-sample checks, and other vision-system validation methods as the case requires
* Define the retraining path for product or process changes
* Report negative results with evidence when the images or the line cannot support the decision

  
**What You'll Bring**

* Several years shipping computer vision into a real operation, not only notebooks and benchmarks
* Factory, AOI, electronics, or other industrial inspection experience
* Experience in PCBA and electronic assembly manufacturing, including IPC workmanship and inspection standards
* Hands-on experience in detection, segmentation, classification, or visual anomaly detection, including labeling, class imbalance, domain shift, and threshold setting
* Ability to evaluate a model on escape rate, false rejects, and cycle time, not only accuracy or mAP

* Ability to work with design engineer, process and quality engineers and turn their defect definitions into a testable problem

As a Machine Learning Engineer (MLE) on the Feed Ranking team, you will own and develop models across our entire ranking stack (Retrieval + Pre-Ranking, Second Pass Ranking, Post-Ranking). Our models are sophisticated (>5B parameters), our features are rich (near-realtime engagement history with 1-year lookback), and our serving requirements are stringent (>10M QPS with low latency and high availability). As an MLE, the reward for working within these requirements is significant - offline performance gains in our ranking models are strongly correlated with topline impact for the entire Eats business.  
  
**What You’ll Do**  

* Own and develop on all parts of the ML lifecycle - both offline (training, model architecture, etc.) and online (serving efficiency, GPU provisioning + utilization, etc.).

*Reports to: Director Data Science + Analytics*  
*Job Type: Full-time W2*

**About the Role**
------------------

We are looking for a pragmatic, hands-on Data Scientist to build and own the quantitative foundation for our clinical care delivery, patient treatment plan refinement, and retention engines.

  

In our specialty care model, clinical health outcomes and business growth are directly linked: matching patients to their preferred, personalized treatment path leads to higher clinical efficacy, better satisfaction, and long-term retention. In this role, you won't just work with clean tabular data; you will bridge the gap between structured clinical metrics (lab values, symptom severity scores, dosage trajectories) and unstructured patient communications (visit transcripts, ambient scribe outputs, and intake survey dialogue).

  

You will sit at the intersection of Data Science, Clinical Operations, and Product, serving as a core builder who transforms messy, multi-modal patient data into actionable clinical decision support and personalized care pathways.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

### **Data Foundation & Pipeline Development**

* **Clean & Transform Multi-Modal Clinical Data:** Build reliable, well-structured modeling tables and feature stores by parsing, cleaning, and joining raw datasets including lab results, symptom severity surveys, medication history, and raw visit transcripts.
* **Establish Unstructured Data Workflows:** Design robust data processing pipelines to convert unstructured clinical notes, orders and visit transcripts into structured, queryable relational tables.

### **Transcript Mining & Feature Extraction**

* **Extract Patient Intent & Preference:** Build lightweight NLP and LLM-based pipelines (using entity extraction, sentiment analysis, and topic modeling) to convert ambient visit transcripts into structured features. And provide insights into patient preferences in treatment pathway, communication, and modality, etc.
* **Identify Friction Points:** Process qualitative dialogue to automatically detect unaddressed obstacles or early side-effect reports before they lead to treatment discontinuation.

### **Lookalike Cohorts & Patient Treatment Planning**

* **Lookalike Clustering Engine:** Develop unsupervised segmentation models to cluster patients into "lookalike" cohorts based on baseline lab values, symptom profiles, and transcript-derived preferences.
* **Outcome & Trajectory Forecasting:** Build predictive models that estimate symptom reduction, time-to-relief, and potential side-effect risks across alternative treatment branches (e.g., immediate HRT vs. conservative step-therapy).

### **Causal Inference & Retention Analytics**

* **Quasi-Experimentation on Care Protocols:** Apply observational study methods (Propensity Score Matching, Difference-in-Differences, Survival Analysis) to evaluate non-randomized care pathways and quantify counterfactual patient outcomes.
* **Drop-Off & Retention Optimization:** Identify critical clinical touchpoints and dosage adjustment milestones that drive long-term program adherence, connecting clinical milestone achievement directly to patient retention and LTV.

### **Research & Cross-Functional Collaboration**

* **Evidence Generation:** Partner with the clinical research team to provide analytical support for peer-reviewed medical publications, white papers, and payer studies.
* **Clinical Operations Alignment:** Translate analytical findings, treatment protocol insights, and patient drop-off trends into actionable workflow improvements for clinical operations and care teams.

**What You Bring**
------------------

### **Technical Skills**

* **Programming & Querying:** Advanced proficiency in SQL for data manipulation alongside strong Python skills for predictive modeling and data transformation.
* **Machine Learning & Modeling:** Practical experience applying clustering (segmentation), regression/classification, and survival analysis (e.g., scikit-learn, statsmodels, lifelines).
* **NLP & Modern LLM Workflows:** Hands-on experience with NLP techniques and LLM frameworks (e.g., transformers, Claude API, etc.) to parse, extract, and classify unstructured text data.
* **Causal Inference Fundamentals:** Solid working knowledge of quasi-experimental design, propensity score matching, and counterfactual reasoning on observational datasets.

### **Analytical Capabilities**

* **Healthcare Data Intuition:** Comfort working with messy, semi-structured, or missing healthcare datasets (lab results, Patient-Reported Outcome Measures/PROMs, EHR notes).
* **Pragmatic "0-to-1" Builder Mindset:** You enjoy doing the foundational data architecture work—cleaning JSON outputs, structuring features, and validating baseline models—before reaching for complex algorithms.
* **Cross-Functional Communication:** Ability to translate technical modeling outcomes into clear, intuitive insights for Clinical Operations and Product partners.

### **Experience**

* 2 to 4 years of hands-on data science or analytics experience delivering high-impact solutions.
* Experience working with healthcare, telehealth, digital health datasets.
* Demonstrated track record of parsing unstructured text/transcript data into structured modeling pipelines.
* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Biomedical Data Science, Health Informatics, Biostatistics, or a related quantitative field.

### **About Mecka AI**

Mecka AI is building the data infrastructure layer for robotics and embodied AI.  
We design and operate global systems for data capture, data labeling, and hardware-enabled workflows used by leading AI labs and robotics companies to train and validate humanoid and embodied AI systems.  
We work closely with frontier robotics teams to bridge real-world data, simulation, learning-based systems, and deployed hardware.

**The role**

You'll take arms we buy off the shelf and make them safely, precisely controllable by an operator thousands of kilometers away. Many of these arms ship with no teleop stack and no teleop input device, so you'll choose and integrate the operator hardware, write the mapping from human motion to robot motion, and own everything that runs on the robot. You'll also be the person who makes sure every frame of data we record is correctly timestamped and synchronized.

**What you'll do**

* Integrate new commercial arms and grippers: vendor SDKs, drivers, calibration, and a common control interface.
* Evaluate and integrate operator input devices (leader arms, VR controllers, 6-DoF mice, haptics).
* Write and tune inverse kinematics and Cartesian/joint controllers for high DOF robotic arms for teleoperation and manipulation.
* Design for latency you can't remove: local safety limits, workspace and collision constraints, graceful handling of dropped or late packets, and safe stop when the link degrades.
* Prototype shared-autonomy features (assisted grasping, motion smoothing, task-level primitives) that make long-distance teleop faster and less tiring.
* Own sensor integration: cameras, depth, wrist cams, joint state, force/torque. Get time synchronization right across all of them.
* Work with a Teleop Platform Engineer on the end-to-end latency budget and on what we record, at what rate, in what format.
* Go to robot sites when needed to bring up hardware and debug in person.

**What we're looking for**

* 3+ years writing production level software that runs real robot hardware (arms strongly preferred), in industry or a serious research lab.
* Strong in C++ and/or Python; comfortable with Linux, real-time considerations, and debugging at the hardware boundary.
* Solid grasp of manipulator kinematics: forward/inverse kinematics, Jacobians, singularities, joint limits, and at least one way of doing Cartesian control well.
* Experience with a robotics middleware stack (e.g., ROS 2) or a good reason you chose not to use one.
* You've integrated a robot from a vendor SDK, not just in simulation.
* Comfortable owning safety-relevant code and being careful about it.

**Nice to have**

* Built a teleoperation system before, especially over unreliable or long-distance networks.
* Experience with impedance/admittance control, force feedback, or haptics.

* Build production forecasting of peak demand, by region and by product, driven by product changes and events rather than trend alone. Quantify uncertainty and track accuracy against actuals
* Model failures and their impact, including correlated and cascading failures. Size the buffers we hold against failures and demand surges, and express plans as risk and cost trade-offs leadership can choose between

------------------

We are looking for a pragmatic, hands-on Data Scientist to build and own the quantitative foundation for our clinical care delivery, patient treatment plan refinement, and retention engines.

  

In our specialty care model, clinical health outcomes and business growth are directly linked: matching patients to their preferred, personalized treatment path leads to higher clinical efficacy, better satisfaction, and long-term retention. In this role, you won't just work with clean tabular data; you will bridge the gap between structured clinical metrics (lab values, symptom severity scores, dosage trajectories) and unstructured patient communications (visit transcripts, ambient scribe outputs, and intake survey dialogue).

  

You will sit at the intersection of Data Science, Clinical Operations, and Product, serving as a core builder who transforms messy, multi-modal patient data into actionable clinical decision support and personalized care pathways.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

### **Data Foundation & Pipeline Development**

* **Clean & Transform Multi-Modal Clinical Data:** Build reliable, well-structured modeling tables and feature stores by parsing, cleaning, and joining raw datasets including lab results, symptom severity surveys, medication history, and raw visit transcripts.
* **Establish Unstructured Data Workflows:** Design robust data processing pipelines to convert unstructured clinical notes, orders and visit transcripts into structured, queryable relational tables.

### **Transcript Mining & Feature Extraction**

* **Extract Patient Intent & Preference:** Build lightweight NLP and LLM-based pipelines (using entity extraction, sentiment analysis, and topic modeling) to convert ambient visit transcripts into structured features. And provide insights into patient preferences in treatment pathway, communication, and modality, etc.
* **Identify Friction Points:** Process qualitative dialogue to automatically detect unaddressed obstacles or early side-effect reports before they lead to treatment discontinuation.

### **Lookalike Cohorts & Patient Treatment Planning**

* **Lookalike Clustering Engine:** Develop unsupervised segmentation models to cluster patients into "lookalike" cohorts based on baseline lab values, symptom profiles, and transcript-derived preferences.
* **Outcome & Trajectory Forecasting:** Build predictive models that estimate symptom reduction, time-to-relief, and potential side-effect risks across alternative treatment branches (e.g., immediate HRT vs. conservative step-therapy).

### **Causal Inference & Retention Analytics**

* **Quasi-Experimentation on Care Protocols:** Apply observational study methods (Propensity Score Matching, Difference-in-Differences, Survival Analysis) to evaluate non-randomized care pathways and quantify counterfactual patient outcomes.
* **Drop-Off & Retention Optimization:** Identify critical clinical touchpoints and dosage adjustment milestones that drive long-term program adherence, connecting clinical milestone achievement directly to patient retention and LTV.

### **Research & Cross-Functional Collaboration**

* **Evidence Generation:** Partner with the clinical research team to provide analytical support for peer-reviewed medical publications, white papers, and payer studies.
* **Clinical Operations Alignment:** Translate analytical findings, treatment protocol insights, and patient drop-off trends into actionable workflow improvements for clinical operations and care teams.

**What You Bring**
------------------

### **Technical Skills**

* **Programming & Querying:** Advanced proficiency in SQL for data manipulation alongside strong Python skills for predictive modeling and data transformation.
* **Machine Learning & Modeling:** Practical experience applying clustering (segmentation), regression/classification, and survival analysis (e.g., scikit-learn, statsmodels, lifelines).
* **NLP & Modern LLM Workflows:** Hands-on experience with NLP techniques and LLM frameworks (e.g., transformers, Claude API, etc.) to parse, extract, and classify unstructured text data.
* **Causal Inference Fundamentals:** Solid working knowledge of quasi-experimental design, propensity score matching, and counterfactual reasoning on observational datasets.

### **Analytical Capabilities**

* **Healthcare Data Intuition:** Comfort working with messy, semi-structured, or missing healthcare datasets (lab results, Patient-Reported Outcome Measures/PROMs, EHR notes).
* **Pragmatic "0-to-1" Builder Mindset:** You enjoy doing the foundational data architecture work—cleaning JSON outputs, structuring features, and validating baseline models—before reaching for complex algorithms.
* **Cross-Functional Communication:** Ability to translate technical modeling outcomes into clear, intuitive insights for Clinical Operations and Product partners.

* Experience working with healthcare, telehealth, digital health datasets.
* Demonstrated track record of parsing unstructured text/transcript data into structured modeling pipelines.
* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Biomedical Data Science, Health Informatics, Biostatistics, or a related quantitative field.
